Hi Priya — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Below is a concise options matrix to start with; I dropped Ben on the thread to share formal pricing and a short MAP (mutual action plan) doc.

Quick answers up front:
- Discount bands (illustrative): 12mo = 10% off on-demand, 24mo = 18%, 36mo = 26% (higher for larger GPU pools). Exact numbers scale with committed GPU-months.
- Phased start / staged ramp: yes — we support staged ramp schedules with committed pricing applied pro-rata to the committed capacity once the ramp milestone is met. We also offer an initial breathing buffer (up to 30 days) to align provisioning.
- Throughput & SLOs: Dedicated pools come with per-model throughput baselines and a 95th percentile tail-latency SLA (e.g., 200 ms for short prompts on V100/A100 equivalent configs). We publish model-specific profiled baselines in the quote.
- Mid-term decreases: standard reserved commits are firm, but we can include an exchange clause (one-time mid-term swap) or credit toward other Redwood services for 50% of the unused committed term — subject to exec approval.

Option matrix (high level):
- Option A — 12 mo, 6-GPU pool (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), start immediate, ramp 50% in month 1 -> 100% month 2. Discount: ~10%.
- Option B — 24 mo, 12-GPU pool, staged ramp: 25% m1 / 50% m3 / 100% m6. Discount: ~18% + one-time onboarding credit for early sign.
- Option C — 36 mo, 24-GPU pool, flexible start (within 90 days), deeper discount (~26%), includes two free model profiling sessions and a one-time swap option at month 18.

I'll attach a short PDF with example pricing bands and a spreadsheet Ben prepared with the MAP.

Next steps: Ben will send the formal pricing doc and a proposed MAP; if that looks good we can spin up a PoC seat (short-term dedicated slice) while legal circles the MSA.

Thanks — Rachel

Hi Priya — looping in on the legal and commercial points. A few notes from our side we can commit to in the SOW/MSA: 

- Credit for under-utilization: we can include a limited unused-capacity credit if usage stays below 70% for two consecutive quarters; the credit would be 25% of the invoiced committed amount for the unused GPU-months. We'd be open to increasing that threshold with a larger commitment.
- Fixed ramp pricing: we can lock the per-GPU committed rate for the agreed ramp calendar in the SOW (protects you from price movement).
- Assignment clause: standard assignment allowed to an affiliate or with Redwood consent (not to be unreasonably withheld); for M&A situations we can include an explicit transfer path with a short notice period.
- SLA language: we'll provide the exact 95th/99th latency metrics and the credit calculus in the SLO exhibit — I can push a draft this week.

If Option B is your preferred path, Ben and I can prepare a SOW addendum that captures the ramp milestones, the fixed-rate protection, and the under-utilization credit.
